components.description: Line card and RSP/RP blank filler for a Cisco ASR 9000 modular chassis. A plain plate on the line-card envelope with a captive installation screw at each end and nothing else on it. It is a functional part, not trim: the installation guide is explicit that "unoccupied card slots must have a blank filler card installed for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC)", and the high-density 100GE cards additionally require the two-screen A9K-LC-FILR-V2 in the slots around them "for optimal cooling and EMI". An empty slot in a real chassis has one of these in it.
components.name: a9k-slot-cover

components.description: Cisco ASR 9001 fan module. A narrow 2RU-tall module that stands on one side of the fixed-port chassis rather than lying across it - the faceplate is a slotted vent, a STATUS lamp and two captive screws.
components.name: asr-9001-fan

components.description: Cisco ASR 9006 Router fan tray. Six axial 92 mm (3.62 in) fans behind a perforated face, secured by a single captive screw and aligned on two guide pins. The ASR 9006 carries two of these for redundancy, side by side above the card cage and BEHIND A HINGED DOOR - which is why, uniquely in this family, no drawing of this tray exists anywhere: on the chassis master you see the door, not the tray.
components.name: asr-9006-fan

components.description: Cisco ASR 9010 Router fan tray. Twelve axial 120 mm (4.72 in) fans behind a full-width band, with a pull handle across the middle, a grip and a captive screw at each end, a FAN STATUS lamp and a hazard label. The ASR 9010 carries two of these for redundancy and both are required for normal operation - if both are pulled or missing the router raises a critical alarm.
components.name: asr-9010-fan

components.description: Cisco ASR 9901 Router fan tray. One axial fan behind a hex-punched plate, a captive screw on the right flange, a pull handle across the bottom, and a round STATUS lamp with its legend beside it. The ASR 9901 carries three of these in a row across the rear, labelled FAN 2, FAN 1 and FAN 0 left to right, and the chassis pulls air front to back through them.
components.name: asr-9901-fan
components.size-notes: both axes from one source - the "ASR-9901 Rear" master, in a chassis face calibrated on the ASR 9901 data sheet's 439.93 x 87.12 mm body. The three plates come out identical to 0.01 mm at x 4.75, 95.74 and 186.73, so the reading is three measurements of one part rather than one.

components.description: Cisco ASR 9902 Router fan tray. One axial fan behind a hex-punched plate split by a centre rib, a captive screw on the left flange, a pull handle across the top, and a round STATUS lamp with its legend beside it. The ASR 9902 carries three of these in a row across the lower rear, and the chassis pulls air front to back through them. It is NOT the ASR 9903's tray - that one is 93.00 mm wide against this 88.58 and carries a different part number.
components.name: asr-9902-fan
components.size-notes: both axes from one source - the "ASR-9902 Rear" master, in a chassis face calibrated on the data sheet body. Taking one axis from each of two sources is the error that made a Cisco power module 3.66 mm too wide. See provenance.size.

components.description: Cisco ASR 9903 Router fan tray. One axial fan behind a hex-punched plate, a captive screw at the top left, a pull handle across the bottom, a single round status lamp beside an S legend, and the FAN-ASR9903-V01 part number printed bottom-to-top on a white strip down the left. The ASR 9903 carries four of these in a row across the lower rear, and the chassis pulls air front to back through them.
components.name: asr-9903-fan
components.size-notes: both axes from one source - the "ASR-9903 Rear" master, in a chassis face calibrated on the data sheet body. Taking one axis from each of two sources is the error that made a Cisco power module 3.66 mm too wide. See provenance.size.

components.description: Cisco ASR 9910 Router fan tray. Twelve axial 134 mm (5.27 in) fans behind a full-width plate, with a pull handle across the middle, a grip at each end, a FAN STATUS lamp at the left and two hazard labels. The ASR 9910 carries two of these for redundancy; the tray is secured by two captive screws and aligns on two guide pins, and swapping one does not interrupt service.
components.name: asr-9910-fan

components.description: Cisco ASR 9912 Router Switch Fabric Card, first generation. One switch fabric plane for an ASR 9912; the guide notes it is the only FC in the family with a SINGLE fabric ASIC. components.description: Cisco ASR 9922 Router fan tray, version 3. The ASR 9922 carries four of these and the ASR 9912 three; the V3 is the wider tray - Cisco raised it from 16.3 to 17.3 inches and lifted each fan's current rating to 2 A - and it is the tray the 16-port, 20-port and 32-port 100GE line cards require in a 9922.

The cable is CABLE-24T1E1J1: a 100-pin connector at one end plugs into the SPA's front, and the other end carries two 50-pin Telco connectors. components.description: The grey dust cap FS ships in an MTP/MPO port - a 12.8 x 8.1 moulding that fills the port's mouth, with a thin waisted saddle rising off it and a plate across the saddle's end to pull it out by. An OCCUPANT of the aperture it plugs (std/mpo@2 and anything composing it), so it comes out, swaps for a plug, or leaves the port empty. THE ONLY ONE OF THE FOUR CAPS THAT IS NEW: the MPO adapters never drew a cap, so this is read off FS's own product renders rather than moved off an adapter, and every figure it carries is an estimate or a declared modelling choice - see `size-notes` and `provenance.depth`. `common/` for the reason common/lc-boot@1 gives: no standard governs a cap's shape, only the interface it plugs.
components.name: mpo-dust-cap
components.size-notes: THE PIXEL SPANS ARE MEASURED; WHAT THEY ARE A READING OF IS AN INTERPRETATION, NOT SETTLED, which is why both axes say `estimated` and not `photo-measured`. FS's face-on renders of SKU 35510 (the 12x MTP adapter panel) show all twelve ports CAPPED, and nothing in them draws a line between the cap's own outline and the mouth of the aperture it stands in. The panel mounts its adapters PORTRAIT, so the render's vertical reading is this part's width and its horizontal reading is its height. ORTHOGRAPHIC FIRST, because a reading off a perspective render is worth nothing whatever it is a reading of. The six ports of the lower row fit a straight line at a pitch of 81.850 px with a largest residual of 0.68 px - under 1% of the pitch - and a least-squares quadratic term of -0.036 px per index squared, which over the whole row is under a pixel. Both rows read the same size to the pixel (74-75 px by 46-47 px, twelve ports), which a perspective view of a 35 mm-tall plate could not give. Nothing here is fitted to a curve because there is no curve to fit. THE SCALE IS THE RENDER'S OWN PRINTED DIMENSION: the plate spans 633 px against its printed 4.29 in (108.97 mm), 5.809 px/mm, cross-checked on the printed 1.38 in height (35.05 mm), which reads 205 px, 5.848 px/mm - the two 0.67% apart. THE SPANS: each port's content measures 74.5 px on the long axis (74-75 across all twelve, both rows, on two renders of the same panel) and 47 px on the short (46-47), which at 5.809 px/mm is 12.82 and 8.09. Inside that sits a brighter block of 59 by 21 px, 10.16 by 3.62. WHICH OF THE TWO THE CAP IS. That the bright block is the WHOLE cap, sitting in a mouth the 12.82 x 8.09 content outlines, is EXCLUDED: a cap 3.62 on its short axis cannot seal an opening std/mpo@2 gives as 8.0, and the oblique renders show a saddle standing off every port, which is what a bright block in the middle of a port looks like seen end-on. So the content is read as the cap's face. IT IS CLOSE TO THE CORRECTED MOUTH, AND THAT AGREEMENT IS PARTLY BY CONSTRUCTION, so it is not evidence for this reading: this same 12.82 x 8.09 is one of the readings that chose the upper end of the clearance std/mpo@2 was derived with (the way standards.yaml's `mpo-plug` note says its own agreement with `mpo-adapter` is by construction). Axis by axis it does not even match: 0.08 inside std/mpo@2's 12.9 on the long axis and 0.09 over its 8.0 on the short. WHAT IS NOT EXCLUDED is that some of the 12.82 x 8.09 is the mouth's own bevel rather than the cap; if a drawing ever settles the cap, this part gets smaller and not larger.

components.description: Hot-swappable fan module for the Edgecore AGR400 (AS7946-30XB) and AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB). Five across the rear in a 4+1 redundant arrangement, numbered FAN 0 at the right to FAN 4 at the left. Two counter-rotating rotors in tandem behind a circular honeycomb finger guard, with a red D-handle on the left of the faceplate.
components.name: agr-fan

components.description: Removable bottom air filter for the Edgecore AGR400 (AS7946-30XB) and AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB). A dark metal frame with open sections and reticulated foam behind them. It bolts onto the OUTSIDE of the faceplate with captive thumb screws - it does not slide into a bay - so it is placed, not seated. A plain rectangle, wider than the top filter because it also spans the SFP28 pair.
components.name: agr-filter-bottom

components.description: Removable top air filter for the Edgecore AGR400 (AS7946-30XB). NOT the AGR420's: that chassis measured this part and rejected it - 353.5 mm against the 417 its front needs, and stepped for the AGR400's TWO QSFP-DD blocks where the AGR420 front has one. The AGR420 draws edgecore/agr420-filter-top@1 with agr420-filter-step@1 instead. A dark metal frame with open sections and reticulated foam behind them. It bolts onto the OUTSIDE of the faceplate with captive thumb screws - it does not slide into a bay - so it is placed, not seated. Its outline is not a plain rectangle - it drops deeper over each QSFP-DD block, which the maintainer describes as two nubs and the photographs confirm.
components.name: agr-filter-top

components.description: Chassis grounding landing on the AGR400/AGR420 rear, between the PSU bay and the fans. An IEC 60417-5019 earth symbol above a two-hole plate for a two-hole grounding lug.
components.name: agr-ground-plate

components.description: Caution label near the rear left of the top cover on the Edgecore AGR400 / AGR420.
components.name: agr-label-caution

components.description: Serial number, SKU and MAC label on the top cover on the Edgecore AGR400 / AGR420.
components.name: agr-label-serial

components.description: Regulatory and specification label on the top cover on the Edgecore AGR400 / AGR420.
components.name: agr-label-spec

components.description: Captive slotted thumb screw at each corner of the Edgecore AGR400 / AGR420 front panel, holding the rack flange to the chassis. A bright plated head about 8.4 mm across with a single broad slot, standing proud of the paint. Much larger than common/screw-head, which is 3.6 mm and reads as a machine screw rather than a thumb screw at this scale.
components.name: agr-panel-screw

components.description: AC-DC hot-swappable PSU for the Edgecore AGR400 (AS7946-30XB) and AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB). Same shell as the DC unit with an IEC C14 appliance inlet in place of the terminal block.
components.name: agr-psu-ac

attrs.input: -40 to -75 VDC, 40 A max per PSU

components.description: DC-DC hot-swappable PSU for the Edgecore AGR400 (AS7946-30XB) and AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB). Black bail handle on the left, a two-post -48 V terminal block in the middle and a red latch on the right. This is the unit we photographed.
components.name: agr-psu-dc

components.description: Removable BOTTOM air filter for the Edgecore AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB) - the full-width band of it. The mirror of the top filter and shorter, stopping at panel x 412 rather than running under the management corner. The same physical filter also carries a deeper section beside the QSFP-DD column, which is agr420-filter-step.
components.name: agr420-filter-bottom

components.description: The deep section of an Edgecore AGR420 air filter, beside the QSFP-DD column at the left of the front panel, where the nearest port row is 17 mm away and the frame can drop a second foam cell in. Both the top and the bottom filter carry one; it is not a separate FRU, it is the stepped end of one, split out because a placement is a bounding rectangle.
components.name: agr420-filter-step

components.description: Removable TOP air filter for the Edgecore AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB) - the full-width band of it. A dark metal frame with open sections and reticulated foam behind them, bolted onto the OUTSIDE of the faceplate with two captive thumb screws; it does not slide into a bay, so it is placed, not seated. The same physical filter also carries a deeper section beside the QSFP-DD column, which is agr420-filter-step.
components.name: agr420-filter-top

components.description: The 2000 W AC power supply of the Edgecore AGR560 (AS9947-36XKB), sold as the FRU PS-2202-8L - a 73.5 x 40 CRPS shell carrying a Lite-On fan at the left with its rating printed on the rotor hub, an IEC 60320 C14 inlet at the right, a pull handle across the foot of the fan guard and the release latch on the right edge. NOT the AIS800-64D's supply: that one is 3000 W on a C20 inlet in a 36 mm guard, and this is 2000 W on a C14 in a 41.9 mm guard. The two share a bay size and nothing else.
components.name: agr560-psu-ac

components.description: The 2000 W -48 VDC power supply of the Edgecore AGR560 (AS9947-36XKB), sold as the FRU DD-2202-1L - the AC unit's 73.5 x 40 shell and Lite-On fan with a TWO-STUD terminal block where that one has a C14 inlet. Two studs, not the six of the AIS800-64D's DC supply: this machine is half the power and its cable is #6 AWG where that one's is #4.
components.name: agr560-psu-dc

components.description: The 3000 W AC power supply of the Edgecore AIS800-64D and AIS800-64O - a CRPS-form module in a bright housing with an octagonal wire fan guard at its left, a black pull loop hanging under the guard, an IEC C20 inlet standing on its side at the right and a coloured release latch down the inlet's right edge. Two stack one above the other at the left of the rear. NOT the 32-port models' supply: that one is 53.7 wide with a Saf-D-Grid; this one is 73.5 wide and the datasheet names the inlet "IEC 60320 C20".
components.name: ais800-64-psu-ac

components.description: The 3000 W DC power supply of the Edgecore AIS800-64D and AIS800-64O - the AC unit's 73.5 x 40 CRPS shell with a six-stud terminal block in place of the fan guard and inlet: two rows of three M-studs under a lifting cover, honeycomb fields either side, a black pull loop standing at the left and the coloured release latch at the right. Drawn from the quick start guide's own Connect Power figure of this face.
components.name: ais800-64-psu-dc

components.description: A rear fan module of the Edgecore AIS800-32D and AIS800-32O - a honeycomb-grilled black tray with a large coloured U-bail across its lower half and one unlabelled lamp at its top left. SEVEN fill this chassis in a 6+1 arrangement, which is one more bay than any other tray in this library's Edgecore rears, and at 41.65 mm it is the narrowest of them.
components.name: ais800-fan

components.description: The 2400 W AC power supply of the Edgecore AIS800-32D and AIS800-32O - a bright CRPS-style module with a latticed grille across its left half, a coloured U-bail hinged down its left edge, one unlabelled lamp at its top left corner, an Anderson Saf-D-Grid appliance inlet standing upright at its right and a small release tab at the bottom right. NOT an IEC inlet: 2400 W on a 200 V line is 12 A continuous and the vendor names the connector outright.
components.name: ais800-psu-ac

components.description: The 2400 W DC power supply of the Edgecore AIS800-32D and AIS800-32O - a bright CRPS-style module with a coloured bail stowed across its top, a ground stud at its top left, a two-pole screw-down barrier block silkscreened -40 - -72 and RTN across its middle, a latticed grille and one unlabelled lamp at its right, and a small release tab at the bottom right. It shares the AIS800's bay with edgecore/ais800-psu-ac@1 and shares none of that module's face.
components.name: ais800-psu-dc

components.description: The Edgecore AMX3200's 1200 W DC supply, ordered as AMX-3200-48V-PSU - a 73.5 x 40.0 module with its release latch at the left edge, its three-pin DC terminal block beside it, its own fan behind a guard at the right, and a black U-handle under the fan. components.size-notes: The faceplate is MEASURED off FS's face-on render of SKU 57058 (57058.main.jpg), scaled on the 108.97 mm FHD module width and validated against the 35.05 mm height to 0.57% - independently reproducing the exact scale check already recorded in standards.yaml's sc-duplex-adapter entry, since this is the same image the adapter body width was measured from. Corroborated by FS's own dimension line on 57058.B.jpg, which reads 4.29in x 1.38in - exactly 108.97 x 35.05, the same reading 57016.B.jpg gives for the LC cassette, confirming both share one FHD faceplate. THE DEPTH IS THE LC CASSETTE'S TOO. 57058.B.jpg's own depth line reads 4.64in, 117.86 mm. Until this contract's 1.5.2 this paragraph set that against a 4.34in on 57016.B.jpg and called the SC body 7.62 mm deeper, with an SC adapter's proud ferrule and shutter offered as the reason. The 4.34in was a misreading: 57016.B.jpg reads 4.64in as well, and fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-os2-a@4 now carries 117.86. There was never a difference to explain, and a physical reason was found for it anyway - which is the thing worth remembering about this paragraph.

components.size-notes:
NOT MEASURED, AND NOT MEASURABLE FROM WHAT IS HELD - the identical situation fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-rear@3 already documents for SKU 57016, and the same numbers are reused rather than re-guessed, for a reason stronger than "the family shares a rear": 57058.D.jpg is the only rear view held here too, it is the same top-rear three-quarter composition, and panel_measure refuses it at 3.7694450%, the SAME figure (independently reproduced) that 57016.D.jpg gives - to four significant figures, not just "close". Two independent SKUs' rear renders failing panel_measure's own scale-validity check by the identical percentage is strong evidence they were shot from the same rig against the same physical rear tooling, which is exactly what 99.0 x 31.0 already assumes. It still cannot be scaled on the faceplate, because the faceplate OVERHANGS the body - the rear face is the body, and the body is narrower by an amount nobody has measured. 99.0 x 31.0 is proportion read off that render against the known 108.97 x 35.05 front, carried over from fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-rear@3 rather than re-derived. A face-on photograph of the back settles it for either SKU.
NO DEPTH IS DECLARED, AND THAT IS THE READING. This contract is a FACE - the drawing of a back, not a part with a back of its own - and render.py turns a `size.d` on a fixed component into `data-depth`, an aperture as big as the whole face. The kit then builds THAT pit and drops the recesses inside it, because it takes only the innermost cavity of a nest: the estimated `d: 2.0` carried until now swallowed the recesses composed onto this face, so a bulkhead's mouth was not built at all and the whole back sat 2 mm below the cassette's edge in 3D. The depth of the body this face closes belongs to the cassette that carries it - `body.depth` there - and differs between them.

components.description: An LC fibre plug as it is SEATED, front view - the four-tier keyed silhouette of the free plug (provenance.free-state) with its latch compressed into the adapter's keyway, and drawn in the bore's own convention: latch DOWN unrotated, as std/lc-bore@3 and std/lc-bulkhead-bore@1 draw their tongue, so the turn a seat applies carries the latch into the keyway on every host. A body holding the ferrule, and below it the latch column - a 3.3 stem off the body, a 4.3 shoulder standing proud of it, then the 2.3 tab. Occupies an `lc` bore at its `mate` and presents `lc-plug` at its rear for a boot. No depth (provenance.size).
components.name: lc-plug

components.description: A 12-fibre MPO/MTP plug, front view - the 12.5 x 7.6 barrel-ended housing with the MT ferrule standing in its window and the key rib across the top face. UNPINNED: the pins live on the module receptacle this lands in, so this is the female half - stated in `provenance.gender` and not as a field, because the schema carries no key for it yet. Occupies an `mpo` aperture (std/mpo@2 and anything composing it) at its own `mate` point, and presents `mpo-plug` at its rear so a boot or a bare cable can seat there - the shape generic/lc-plug@2 already has, with nothing built yet to take it up. generic/mpo24-plug@1 is the same housing with a two-row ferrule; the fibre count is a property of the ferrule and not of the outline, which is why they are two parts and not one with an attr.
components.name: mpo12-plug

components.description: A 24-fibre MPO/MTP plug, front view - the SAME 12.5 x 7.6 barrel-ended housing generic/mpo12-plug@1 draws, with a two-row MT ferrule in it. The fibre count is a property of the ferrule and not of the outline, which is why this is its own part rather than an attr on that one (docs/pluggables-design.md, decision 10), and why the two contracts agree figure for figure: nothing outside the ferrule window changes with the row count. UNPINNED, the same way. Occupies an `mpo` aperture (std/mpo@2 and anything composing it) at its own `mate` point, and presents `mpo-plug` at its rear so a boot or a bare cable can seat there.
components.name: mpo24-plug

components.description: A generic QSFP-DD with an LC duplex face - the shape every QSFP-DD, QSFP-DD800 and QSFP112 optic with two LC bores has, standing for all of them. Two keyed bores with the ferrules standing in them, and a pull tab standing proud of the body because the module is seated. Which module it is - rate, reach, wavelength, watts - is a fact about a vendor's product and lives on the wrapper that composes this (docs/pluggables-design.md, decision 5), never here. Copies generic/qsfp-lc@1 and changes the family: same width and height by design (QSFP-DD HW Rev 6.3 section 1 - the QSFP-DD cage accepts a QSFP module), a longer paddle card behind the same front cross-section.
components.name: qsfp-dd-lc

components.description: A generic QSFP with an LC duplex face - the shape every QSFP+, QSFP28 and QSFP56 optic with two LC bores has, standing for all of them. components.description: An RJ45 (8P8C) copper plug, the UNSHIELDED variant - a rectangular body with a spring latch on its underside that engages a jack's latch slot. Occupies a `rj45` receptacle (std/rj45@2 and anything that composes it) at its own `mate` point, and in turn presents `rj45-plug` so a boot (or a bare cable, when there is no boot) can seat on its rear. UNLIKE generic/lc-plug@2, this plug HAS a class-wide depth - see `provenance.size`.
components.name: rj45-plug

components.description: An SC fibre plug, front view - the square keyed silhouette an SC connector presents end-on: a 7.4 x 9.0 housing with the 2.5 mm ferrule on its axis and a 0.9 x 1.8 key standing off one long wall, drawn to the LEFT unrotated so it enters std/sc-bore@1, whose keyway is on the left unrotated too. Occupies an `sc` receptacle (std/sc-bore@1 and anything composing it) at its own `mate` point, and in turn presents `sc-plug` so a boot (or a bare cable) can seat on its rear - the shape generic/lc-plug@2 already has, with no `common/sc-boot` built yet to take it up. Drawn with NO depth - see `provenance.size` - but standing out of its opening in 3D by an estimated standoff, `provenance.standoff`.

components.description: Smartoptics DCP-404 muxponder, a half-width 1RU plug-in unit for one DCP-2 traffic slot. Each port carries its number, a Tx/Rx caption with a green lamp beside each word, and a hex vent group above the cage. components.name: ppm-ad1-1510

components.description: Smartoptics PPM-AD1-1625-2F - a passive plug-in module that adds and drops a 1625nm OTDR signal onto the line fibre, so a fibre break can be located without taking the traffic wavelengths down. components.description: F-type 75-ohm coaxial panel jack (3/8-32 UNEF-2A) - the CATV drop connector. The threaded neck IS the mating interface, so it stands proud of the panel with the hex nut clamped behind it; the aperture is a double-D hole.
components.name: f-type

components.description: One LC receptacle bore - the KEYED opening an LC plug enters, not a square hole. Four tiers on one axis - the square bore with the fiber ferrule standing in it, then a neck, a shoulder and a latch tongue that together clear the plug's latch arm. Tongue down when unrotated; rotate 180 at placement for a receptacle fitted latch-up, which is how every receptacle in the corpus is drawn.
components.name: lc-bore

components.description: One LC bore of a BULKHEAD (panel-mount) adapter - the keyed opening an LC plug enters, with the full-length keyway a panel adapter carries. The same square, widths and mate as std/lc-bore@3, which is the TRANSCEIVER receptacle and draws a keyway cut short to fit a module face; this part is the bulkhead aperture, and its latch stack is the one measured off SENKO's LC Premium Adapter. Tongue down when unrotated, the convention std/lc-bore@3 keeps; a placement turns it.
components.name: lc-bulkhead-bore

components.description: MCX coaxial panel jack (IEC 61169-36) - snap-on micro coax, the 75-ohm RF drop connector on cable headend I/O cards and the 50-ohm GNSS/timing jack elsewhere. The panel aperture is a D-hole with one anti-rotation flat.
components.name: mcx

components.description: Micro-USB Type-B receptacle, as used for a console port
components.name: micro-usb

components.description: One MPO/MTP adapter opening - the mouth an MPO plug enters, not the adapter around it. The panel-mount part that carries a bezel is common/mpo-adapter@2, which composes this. Shared by MPO-8, -12 and -24 because fibre count is a property of the ferrule rather than of the opening. 12.9 x 8.0, ESTIMATED: the printed MPO connector envelope plus a clearance measured on another connector family, because no document held here dimensions the opening itself (provenance.size).
components.name: mpo

components.description: RJ45 modular jack HOUSING - the 15.8 x 13.2 plastic face a plug enters, with the 8P8C interface recessed into solid walls in three tiers (body, latch shoulder, latch slot). Pins up, keyway down when unrotated; rotate 180 at placement for a jack fitted the other way up.
components.name: rj45

components.description: One cell of a shared-wall 2xN RJ45 block - the 12.7 x 11.0 face between neighbouring ports on a 13.97 pitch, with the same three-tier 8P8C interface as the single housing recessed into it. Rows mirror; the upper row is this part rotated 180 at placement.
components.name: rj45-ganged

components.description: Anderson Saf-D-Grid appliance inlet - the panel cutout with the keyed coupler recessed behind it, a first-mate last-break ground above a positive and a negative. It sits in roughly the space an IEC C14 takes and carries several times the current through it, which is why a 1.6 kW supply on a 90 V low line uses one.
components.name: saf-d-grid

components.description: One SC opening - the rectangular hole an SC plug's housing enters, with the key slot cut into one long wall and the 2.5 mm ferrule standing in its sleeve. Key slot to the LEFT when unrotated. The SC counterpart of std/lc-bore@3: the part a panel adapter composes so the opening is drawn once and drawn right.
components.name: sc-bore
components.size-notes: 7.5 x 9.0 is the opening, printed on SENKO's SC Premium Adapter drawing (DS-SC-000010 Rev A, front view, `7.5 -0.0/-0.1` and `9 +0.1/-0.0`) and cross-checked on its SC TOP Adapter (DS-SC-000011 Rev A), whose front view prints the same 7.5 on its own opening. The extra 0.89 of width is the key slot, and see `provenance.keyway`. The 6.0 depth is not from either drawing: it is deep enough that the ferrule face sits below the opening, which is what looking into an SC port shows.
